description: Per-company, per-state tax configuration. One record per (company x state x tax_year). Oregon: income tax, Statewide Transit Tax, Paid Leave Oregon, Workers' Compensation. Washington: PFML, WA Cares Fund, L&I. Rates are entered by the employer because they vary by classification and employer size.

fields.description: The employer's account number with this state's revenue agency — Oregon's Business Identification Number (BIN), Washington's ESD account number. Printed on W-2 box 15 and at the head of every state return. v0.34.0.
fields.label: Employer Account Number

fields.description: This employer's own assigned state unemployment insurance rate, as a percentage of taxable wages. EMPLOYER-ONLY and EMPLOYER-ENTERED: the rate comes from the state agency out of this employer's experience rating, so there is no table this app could ship. Left at zero, no SUTA is computed and nothing about the payroll changes. v0.40.0.
fields.label: SUTA Rate

fields.description: Taxable wage base per employee per year, consumed by year-to-date gross the way FUTA's $7,000 is. Oregon's 2025 base is 54300 and Washington's is 72800; both move every year, which is why this is a field. ZERO MEANS NO CAP — every dollar of gross is taxable — which is the honest reading of a rate entered with no base beside it. v0.40.0.
fields.label: SUTA Wage Base
Oregon Income Tax Enabled
fields.description: Enable Oregon state income tax withholding.

fields.label: Statewide Transit Tax Rate
fields.description: Oregon Statewide Transit Tax rate (0.1% for 2025). No wage base cap.

fields.label: Paid Leave Total Rate
fields.description: Total Paid Leave Oregon contribution rate (1.0% for 2025).

fields.label: Employee Share
fields.description: Employee share of the total rate (60% for employers with 25+ employees).

fields.label: Employer Share
fields.description: Employer share of the total rate (40% for employers with 25+ employees).

fields.label: Small Employer (under 25 employees)
fields.description: Employers with fewer than 25 employees do not pay the employer share.

fields.label: Workers' Comp Rate
fields.description: Varies by classification code. Employer-entered.

fields.label: PFML Rate
fields.description: Total PFML rate (0.92% for 2025).

fields.label: Employee Share
fields.description: Employee share of PFML rate (typically ~72.76%).

fields.label: Employer Share
fields.description: Employer share of PFML rate (typically ~27.24%).

fields.label: PFML Wage Base
fields.description: Social Security wage base ($176,100 for 2025).

fields.label: WA Cares Rate
fields.description: WA Cares Fund premium rate (0.58% for 2025). Employee-only.

fields.label: Employee Only
fields.description: WA Cares is 100% employee-paid. Employer pays nothing.

fields.label: Exempt Employees
fields.description: Employee IDs who opted out before the deadline. Comma-separated.

fields.label: L&I Employee Rate
fields.description: Varies by risk class. Employer-entered.

fields.label: L&I Employer Rate
fields.description: Varies by risk class. Employer-entered.

The wage floor these hours are owed. It lives HERE rather than in a settings page of its own because a minimum wage is a fact about a state in a year, which is exactly what this record already is — one row per company, state and tax year. Leave every field below at zero and the shipped table applies (Oregon $14.70 standard / $13.70 non-urban / $15.95 Portland metro, Washington $16.66); set one and it wins for this company, this state and this year. That is what makes a July rate change a row somebody edits instead of a release.
fields.label: Minimum Wage

fields.description: The standard hourly floor for this state. Zero means 'not set here' and the shipped table applies — NOT 'this state has no minimum wage', which is a thing no state in this app is. The floor is PAID and not merely reported: gross pay is the greater of what the work earned and what the hours were owed, and the difference appears on the slip as `minimum_wage_makeup`.
fields.label: Minimum Wage (Standard)

fields.description: When this rate took effect, for the record. NOT read by the payroll engine, which selects the configuration by TAX YEAR — a rate change mid-year needs the row for that year updated, and this column is what tells the next person reading it which change they are looking at.
fields.label: Minimum Wage Effective From

fields.description: OREGON ONLY. ORS 653.025 sets three rates by geography, and this is the non-urban counties one. Leave it at zero in any other state — a worker's region is named on their salary structure, and a region a state does not define falls back to the standard rate rather than to nothing.
fields.label: Minimum Wage (Non-Urban)

fields.description: OREGON ONLY. The Portland metro rate under ORS 653.025 — the highest of the three, and the one that applies to work inside the urban growth boundary. Same rule as above: zero means not set, and a state with no such region ignores it.
fields.label: Minimum Wage (Portland Metro)
